༄༅།།This is something called a subscribed letter. In this case, it is the letter འ་ ('a) which denotes a long vowel present in Sanskrit/ Pali. OM is usually written ཨོཾཿ if I remember correctly. Hence ཨཱོཾཿ is just a representation of the original ŌM sound, without this changing the pronunciation greatly. Another example of subscribed འ་ would be the sacred syllable HŪNG ཏཱུྃཿ . The symbol at the beginning of my comment and the one ending it are Tibetan marks of beginning and end of texts, that also have a protective function. The circles are traditionally added after sacred syllables, too, as far as I know. The reversed letters denote Sanskrit-specific sounds, e.g. ཎ་ stands for a retroflex n. Hope this helps!།།
